current.text: Sengun is a projected starter for Houston, with VanVleet, Thompson, Durant and Smith.
Coach Ime Udoka has blamed Sengun's defense for years and limits his minutes. Other bigs sometimes play over him.
With more guard depth, his minutes could drop from about 33 to 31 or 32.
Fred VanVleet is back from injury. Sengun's assists were boosted while VanVleet was out.
His assists should fall to about 5 to 5.5 per game. Last season was already his best shot-blocking year, so there is no blocks upside to make up for it.
Experts value him at about 30 USD in auctions and rank him around 24 to 30 in category leagues. They call his ADP reasonable.
With a March 28 end, Houston plays a weak 3-3-4 schedule in our fantasy playoff weeks, 10 games over three weeks.
Houston has only 14 back-to-backs this season.
Houston is projected to win about 54 games and is expected to stay conservative in the regular season rather than chase seeding.

durable.text: Sengun is a two-time All-Star who can put up about 20 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists.
He has an unusual stat line for a big: a strong assist boost plus steals and blocks, with good FG%.
He is a poor free throw shooter, and on his volume it clearly hurts a team's FT%.
He makes almost no threes, and his three-point shot will probably never come around.
He commits about 3 turnovers per game, which is a weak outlier in the league and for his position.
He is not a big shot blocker.
His defense is a concern. Other weaknesses are finishing at the rim, overall efficiency, too many low-percentage mid-range shots and complaining to officials.
He is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues.
Last season he missed time with back tightness and then an ankle injury. He wore down in mid-season after playing EuroBasket.

note: Sengun went for 36 USD in our league last season. Yahoo values him at 32 USD and ESPN at 26 USD, while both sites' average costs sit near 32 USD and experts put him near 30 USD, so paying more than about 30 USD means paying points-league prices for a 9-cat player. He fits punt FT% and punt TO builds best: his FT% (69% on about 5.5 attempts) and about 3 turnovers per game are the drags, and assists from the C spot, rebounds and good FG% are the gains. Early in the season, check whether his minutes stay near 33 or slip to 31 under Udoka, and whether his assists drop toward 5 with VanVleet back. Also keep in mind that Houston has only 10 games across our playoff weeks.
